text:
mikhail: Hey all, after upgrading to py-sdk 0.7.0 I’m seeing a steady growth of TCP connections in CLOSE_WAIT on our app nodes when using the AsyncClient.

mikhail: Repro steps: spawn 200 coroutines that call client.generate(...) concurrently, then wait for them to finish and sleep the loop for ~30s. After a few cycles sockets pile up.

mikhail: Minimal snippet:```\nfrom redwood import AsyncClient\n\nasync def call_once(client):\n    await client.generate(prompt='hi')\n\nasync def run():\n    client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))\n    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(call_once(client)) for _ in range(200)]\n    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)\n    await asyncio.sleep(30)\n```\n\nmikhail: Observed in strace/lsof: a bunch of connections in CLOSE_WAIT and connection count never drops until process restart. Not seeing same behavior on 0.6.x.

sara: ugh. can you paste the httpx/uvloop versions? also which transport is used (any custom)?

mikhail: httpx 0.24.1, uvloop 0.17.0, linux sockstat shows TIME_WAIT->CLOSE_WAIT transitions. No custom transport.

eli: sounds like keepalive/drain timing got changed. We adjusted the async pool to avoid early socket churn but maybe the idle-drain task isn't closing on loop stop. Can you try setting AsyncClient(pool_keepalive=5) and see?

mikhail: tried pool_keepalive=5 (and 0) — still see leak over minutes. but if I explicitly call await client.aclose() the sockets go away.

eli: OK that suggests session lifecycle hooks aren't firing or the background reaper task is detached. Can you run with RDW_DEBUG=1 and post the SDK logs? also which GC cycle frequency?

mikhail: tossed logs:```\n[rdw.sdk] INFO reaper starting interval=60s\n[rdw.sdk] DEBUG connpool: connection returned to pool id=0x1f, state=idle\n[rdw.sdk] DEBUG connpool: reaper check elapsed=60000ms\n[rdw.sdk] WARN connpool: idle conn age 120s exceeds keepalive=60s but socket still open\n```\n\nmikhail: After about 10 reaper cycles connections still stuck, reaper keeps reporting socket open but we never see closed events.

sara: can you try a workaround: create client per-batch and aclose after gather? i know it's less efficient but helps isolate. if that works it’s lifecycle bug for persistent client.

mikhail: per-batch client creation eliminates the leak. so yes lifecycle of long-lived client is implicated.

eli: filing an issue. @devx-bot can you create GH issue with labels: sdk, bug, high-pri and link logs? include a minimal snippet and steps.

devx-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/482 — title: "AsyncClient idle drain task not closing sockets after upgrade to 0.7.0". Assigned to @eli.

sara: temporary patch: if you want to keep long-lived client, you can spawn a periodic await client._transport.aclose() every 30s as a hack (danger: internal API). not ideal.

mikhail: thanks. will revert to 0.6.x in prod for now and test a 0.7.1 candidate from the issue branch.

eli: we’ll prioritize a fix — likely cause is reaper task not awaiting socket close on async backends. will post update in the issue and in this thread.

mikhail: appreciate it. Will share perf numbers if useful. :thumbsup:
